newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs recover from lows, gains capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs recover from lows, gains capped.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures recovered from their lows in late Tuesday trade but dealers said rises were likely to be capped.
Euroyen futures were dragged down by a sharp drop in JGB futures in early trade, which in turn came under pressure from supply concerns and large-lot sales in Tokyo.
"The early selling of JGBs was due to several corporate bond issues. There were concerns about excess supply," a trader with a European futures house said.
He said the drop in JGB futures was exacerbated by sales from hedge funds, said to be holding a large number of June JGB put options with a strike price of 123.00.
"I heard the hedge funds were in the market. One fund sold 700 lots of June JGBs on the TSE (Tokyo Stock Exchange)," the trader said.
He said stop-loss sales were triggered below the 123.00 level pushing the contract down to a low of 122.80 from its opening 123.64. It recovered to close at 123.29 against 123.67 previously.
"I think the JGBs will remain under pressure. The expectations of a rate hike are still there," the trader said, adding that June JGBs could test support at 122.75 again.
He said last Friday's comments by key Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, on the possibility of a rate hike, continued to weigh on the market.
Sakakibara told the French afternoon daily, Le Monde, in an interview the Bank of Japan could be expected to hike its discount rate by 0.50 percent in the coming year.
The lead December Euroyen contract was quoted at 98.86 at 1115 GMT after falling to a low of 98.84 against its IMM close at 98.87 on volume of 15,720 lots.
"My strategy would be to sell the Euroyen on any rallies. I think 98.90 would be a good level to sell," a trader with a U.S. futures house said.
Eurodollar futures ended flat in light trade as the market lacked leads after a U.S. holiday on Monday. September ended at 93.970 against an opening 93.975 on volume of 3,050 lots.
